column_semantics: The schedule uses a single column headed Interest. For floating-rate PIK debt, the displayed reference-rate spread is the cash spread and the PIK component is printed separately in parentheses in the same Interest cell, e.g. SR + 6.25% (2.75% PIK). Thus the stated spread excludes the PIK component, which is additive. For fixed-rate PIK-only instruments, the Interest cell prints the PIK rate directly, e.g. 9.00% PIK or 11.25% PIK.

rationale: The decisive target-quarter evidence is the Interest column's additive formatting. Floating-rate PIK positions print a cash reference-rate spread followed by a separate parenthetical PIK rate, such as SR + 6.25% (2.75% PIK), SR + 5.75% (2.00% PIK), and SR + 7.25% (2.50% PIK). Because the PIK component is separately stated after the spread, the spread is not an all-in coupon. Fixed-rate PIK-only positions print only the PIK rate with the PIK label, which is consistent with the same component-specific convention rather than an all-in total column.
